column1: # The committed parity corpus (ADR 0008): every VIN list on main when it was
# assembled, plus every deviation witness. scripts/oracle.sh decodes it on the
# freshened oracle into answer-key.csv beside it, and pkg/decoder's TestParity
# holds the engine to that key; manifest.json records the run. The refresh
# carries this file to the next month's directory, appending new witnesses
# (scripts/oracle.sh corpus), and re-freezes the key (go test -update-parity).
# Format: one VIN per line, optionally a tab and a model-year hint; blank lines
# and lines starting with # are skipped. A (VIN, hint) pair appears once.
# Sources, in order: testdata/oracle/sample-vins.tsv, then pkg/decoder's
# core-vins.tsv, error-vins.tsv, wrapper-vins.tsv and ultravin-vins.tsv, each
# section keeping its own comments; then every hinted VIN once more without a
# hint. The ultravin section is the VIN list of ultravin
# dbc9777: the 434 VINs of its frozen parity corpus (tests/parity_corpus.json),
# then the VINs of its cover set (cover_vins() of its 2026_10 artifact) that the
# corpus lacks. Only the VINs are taken; every answer here is our own oracle's.
## pkg/decoder/testdata/core-vins.tsv: chosen for the core pass.
# Non-ASCII input: Postgres keeps the rune, sanitize writes '&'. In a
# wildcard key position both match; in a literal or bracket position
# neither does; in the WMI the decode stops at code 7; ı and ſ upper-case
# C8, decided on the third rung, key length without '*' (brackets count):
# AZ2[AB] (7) beats AZ2[ABCD] (9) for element 13, *D43 beats *D[2345] for
# C8, decided on the fourth rung, keys without brackets in byte order:
# C8 on CreatedOn, and a Pattern against a Formula Pattern on priority (one
# VIN with a '#' of its own, which formulaKeys keeps).
# C3: two element-18 items tie on priority and CreatedOn; the later id wins.
# For 1M1MDA… the two are ISL, an engine model with engine model patterns,
# and B6.7, which names none, in one order in 2024's schema and the other
# C3 engine model patterns, with displacements that feed conversions 4 and
# C10 from pattern displacements: conversions 1 and 3 (CC), 5 (CI), 2 (CI).
# C7 formula patterns whose AttributeId is TBD: the conversions raise, '0'.
# C7 formula values: '#' in the input, and a one-digit value.
## pkg/decoder/testdata/error-vins.tsv: chosen for the error codes.
# The stale-cache class's witnesses (docs/deviations/stale-cache.md), at the
# years stock and freshened Postgres pick: the test's oracle is freshened.
# Code 9: a Glider body class (2NP, key *G).
# Code 10: off-road body classes; the scan then skips position 9, here a
# The incomplete-vehicle warning: Vehicle Type 10 (2LJ; 4C9154 also has a
# Clean: code 0. Without a Model item code 14 follows, and with no unused
# position its text is NULL, so element 156 is NULL or only later notes.
# Possible values listing '_', which sorts first (1FT 2023: *F[1268_______];
# A VinException check-digit exemption: no code 1, the note on code 0.
# Code 8: an available WMI with no year band.
# Short input: code 6 from the core; positions past the end are skipped.
# Spaces inside: a kept space drops out of the suggested VIN.
# '?' at position 9 equals fVINCheckDigit's '?'; '_' and '*' elsewhere.
# Non-ASCII where the correction search and the scan echo it back.
## pkg/decoder/testdata/wrapper-vins.tsv: chosen for the decode wrapper.
# W0: 17 characters decode whatever their bytes, and spaces around the
# input are trimmed first. Inputs over 17 characters after trimming raise in
# Postgres (vin is a varchar(17)) and are left out: an answer key cannot hold
# a raise. TestProjectionPostgres checks them against the live procedure.
# The cover set, less the corpus.
## Every hinted VIN above, without a hint.
